and behold, he was there.
And as at that time the roads were opened,
and merchants {OCR?} were travelling from Babel, Assyria, and Persia to Syria,
and Egyptian merchants were coming to these territories of the Tatars,
and no one molested them.
Now, when this Abd al-Rahman prepared to go to Syria,
he took a great quantity of royal treasure of the Mongols:
precious stones, wondrous pearls,
gold and silver,
and garments and pieces of cloth heavily woven with gold.
And he set out from Ala-Taq and came to Tabriz,
and stayed there about a month of days.
And he gathered to himself craftsmen of every kind:
founders, tailors, and so forth,
and prepared everything royal.
And from there he came to Mosul,
and sent and brought from Baghdad ten thousands of gold besides,
and took [it] and went to Mardin.
And there came to him an envoy of the Sultan Alfi, the lord of Egypt, and said to him:
"The Sultan sends greeting to you, and says:
'All this time I have been sitting in Damascus,
and waiting for your arrival,
that I may see you and fulfill your request, and go to Egypt,
because this land cannot bear the numerous troops that are with me.
Therefore I ask
that you do not delay.'"
And this Abd al-Rahman sent word to him:
"Behold, I am prepared to come.
Only, I ask of you
that when I come to your land,
your servants shall bring me to you with honor,
and not conduct me by night,
as they did to those envoys who came to you before me."
And the Sultan sent word to him:
"You are great with us,
and your honor is different from that of these others.
Therefore, gladden your heart,
and come at your ease, however you wish."
Then this Sheikh Abd al-Rahman was encouraged,
and he sent and brought the force of the Tatars who were guarding the roads of Amid,
and they rode with him.
And also the lord of Mardin, Malik Muzaffar, sent an envoy with him from his side, Shams al-Din, who was called Bar Titi,
a great and famous man.
And he also sent other forces,
that they should go in attendance on the Sheikh as far as the Euphrates and return.
And the Sheikh set out from Mardin in the tenth month of the Arabs, which is Shawwal of the year 682 [A.D. 1284],
And when he arrived at the city of Harran,
there came to meet him an emir, one of the servants of the lord of Egypt.
